description:
FILED s409 (Fable review of s408) by three probes vs perl 5.40.3.  All three are
PRE-EXISTING at b7ce704 (verified in a worktree) -- #337 did not cause them; it
made them the LAST uncovered spellings of the lexical-sub rename.

Parser2::_rename_lexical_subs (#337) renames `my sub NAME {BODY}` and the uses
its region owns.  Three spellings perl treats as the SAME lexical are outside
its reach today:

(a) SILENT WRONG -- the FORWARD-DECLARATION idiom, `my sub c; sub c {...}`:

        { my sub c; sub c { "c1" } print c(), " " }
        { my sub c; sub c { "c2" } print c(), "\n" }
        perl: c1 c2      PCL: c2 c2

    The pass skips bodiless declarations (`next if !$st->block`) with a comment
    that the fill-in is "a package-sub token shape" -- so BOTH halves stay
    package subs, and two scopes clobber each other exactly as #337's core bug
    did.  This is the perl-documented idiom for mutually recursive lexical subs
    (perlsub, "my sub baz; sub baz {...}").

(b) DIVERGENCE (wrong value) -- a plain `sub NAME {...}` inside the region of
    `my sub NAME` DEFINES THE LEXICAL in perl (that is what makes (a) work); PCL
    keeps it a package sub and leaves the lexical alone:

        my sub f { "L" }
        { package O; sub f { "M" } }
        print f(), " ", (O->can("f") ? "O::f exists" : "no O::f"), "\n";
        perl: M no O::f      PCL: L O::f exists

    _lexsub_renamable returns 0 for a Word after `sub` unless it is the
    declaration itself.

(c) CRASH (loud) -- a use from ANOTHER PACKAGE's code.  A lexical is file-scoped
    regardless of `package`, but PCL resolves the renamed bareword in the
    CURRENT package:

        my sub helper { "H" }
        package Other;
        sub go { helper() }
        package main;
        print Other::go(), "\n";
        perl: H      PCL: undefined-function pl-helper__lexsub__1 (in Other)

    (Before #337 this also crashed -- `Other::helper` -- so not a regression.)

FIX SHAPE (one pass, three edits; name resolution => THE FULL SWEEP IS THE GATE):
  1. a bodiless `my sub NAME;` / `state sub NAME;` OPENS a region like a bodied
     one (drop the `!$st->block` skip); the declaration itself lowers as it does
     today (a forward declaration of the renamed name).
  2. in _lexsub_renamable, a Word after `sub` that heads a PACKAGE sub statement
     (`PPI::Statement::Sub`, no my/state) INSIDE a covering region is RENAMED --
     it is the lexical's definition, as perl reads it.  That fixes (a) and turns
     (b) into perl's answer when the definition is in the SAME package.
  3. cross-package: rewrite the use to the QUALIFIED renamed name
     (`DeclPkg::NAME__lexsub__N`) when the token's package differs from the
     declaration's -- Parser2 already carries a package-at-token resolver for
     the variable rename family (s378, "package-switch resolver"); reuse it, do
     not add a scope walk (var-handling-review-s379 standing rule).  If that is
     not cheap, (c) may DIE naming the shape (loud today already) -- but (a) and
     (b) are wrong VALUES and must be fixed.
  Guard rows: the three reproducers + the (b) same-package spelling + a
  must-NOT-fire list (a package `sub f` OUTSIDE any region; `sub f;` bodiless
  package forward decl inside a region -- perl: also the lexical? PROBE FIRST).
  Population: grep both populations for `my sub \w+;` (bodiless) -- believed
  perl-tests/sub.t inside eval strings only (#337 note) and t/op/lexsub.t.

Related: #337 (done), #373 (the string-eval seam -- separate: that one is the
capture alist), #341 (op/lexsub.t sizing).  Probe files: the s409 review
scratch p19/p20/p25 (reproducers above are complete).
subject: Lexical-sub rename (#337): three uncovered spellings -- `my sub c; sub c {...}` fwd-decl is SILENT WRONG across two scopes (c2 c2 vs perl c1 c2); a plain `sub NAME` in the region defines the LEXICAL in perl; a use from another package crashes
